# Vendored third-party libraries

These libraries are vendored so the project works without installing
dependencies (`bootstrap()` in `src/common.py` appends `vendor/` to
`sys.path`). A pip install of the pinned versions (see
`requirements-optional.txt`) takes priority at import time — `vendor/` is
appended, not prepended, so pip wins — and the vendored copies stay as the
zero-install fallback. Do **not** modify the PyPI-derived files by hand —
re-run `scripts/update_vendor.sh` instead.

## From PyPI (managed by `scripts/update_vendor.sh`)

| Package     | Version   | PyPI project                          | Upstream source                                  | License    |
|-------------|-----------|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------|
| msgpack     | 1.1.2     | https://pypi.org/project/msgpack/     | https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-python        | Apache 2.0 |
| flatbuffers | 25.12.19  | https://pypi.org/project/flatbuffers/ | https://github.com/google/flatbuffers            | Apache 2.0 |

- `vendor/msgpack/` — retained files: `__init__.py`, `ext.py`, `fallback.py`, `exceptions.py`. License text: `COPYING` (Apache 2.0, from upstream).
- `vendor/flatbuffers/` — retained files: `bootstrap_byte_reader`, `builder`, `compat`, `encode`, `flexbuffers`, `number_types`, `packer`, `table`, `util`, `_version` (all `.py`). License text: `LICENSE` (Apache 2.0, from upstream).

## Project-authored pure fallbacks (project files, not from PyPI)

| File                 | Replaces (pip) | Notes                                                          |
|----------------------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `xxh64_pure.py`      | `xxhash`       | Pure-Python XXH64 (seed 0), only used for short data.i path hashes. |
| `lz4_block_pure.py`  | `lz4`          | Pure-Python LZ4 block decompression (game archive chunks).     |

Selection is centralized in `src/deps/` (`deps.xxh64`, `deps.lz4_block`):
each wrapper prefers the pip build when importable and falls back to these
pure copies. `msgpack` and `flatbuffers` need no wrapper — `sys.path` order
alone selects them. `gbfr_schema` (in `src/`) is generated by flatc
`25.12.19`, so `bootstrap()` forces the vendored flatbuffers when the pip
copy drifts from that pin.

## Verification

- `scripts/update_vendor.sh` re-downloads the pinned wheels and **verifies the
  vendored PyPI files are byte-for-byte identical to them** (md5), failing the
  update on any drift.
- `tests/test_deps.py` asserts the pip builds (msgpack/xxhash/lz4 C
  extensions) behave identically to the pinned pure-Python versions, so a
  drift between the two is caught even when pip is installed.
